cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: AMQP (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) is an open, binary, wire-level protocol defining how apps send to and receive from a message broker, including routing, queueing, acknowledgment and redelivery. RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus, Qpid and ActiveMQ use it.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Producers publish to an exchange, which routes to queues by routing key (fanout, topic, direct, headers). Consumers ACK after processing so the broker can redeliver on failure or send to a dead-letter queue. Pick AMQP for reliable work queues, MQTT for lightweight IoT pub/sub, Kafka for replayable streams, webhooks for simple callbacks.

questions.q: Is a WebSocket or gRPC connection a replacement for a queue?
questions.a: No. They are transports to a service online right now, with no durable storage, retries or dead-letter queues.
Decides which queues a message goes to based on its routing key and exchange type.
So the broker knows processing finished and can redeliver or dead-letter on failure.
